issues.title: publish.yml: PR lookup, permissions, event-field handling and artifact intake are unspecified (pwn-request surface)
issues.problem:
- For fork PRs, `github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests` is empty. The GitHub docs example reads the PR number from an artifact, which lets an attacker make the bot comment on, or edit the sticky comment of, any PR or issue.
- Downloading another run's artifacts needs `actions: read`, which is missing from the design's permission list.
- head_branch, display_title (the PR title) and head_commit.message are attacker-controlled. Interpolating them with `${{ }}` inside a `run:` step is script injection in a job that holds pull-requests: write, and contents: write if it is the same job.
- Finding the sticky comment by marker alone can match the attacker's own comment. A token with pull-requests: write can edit other users' comments.
- actions/download-artifact before v4.1.7 had zip-slip (CVE-2024-42471).
- No size cap before download and no member allow-list are specified.
- actions/checkout v7 (GA 2026-06-18; backported to floating major tags from 2026-07-20) refuses fork head/merge checkouts in workflow_run when the triggering event is pull_request*. Submission files must be fetched as data.
issues.recommendation:
- Trigger: `on: workflow_run: {workflows: [eval], types: [completed]}`, with a job-level guard `if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`. Also check `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/eval.yml'`; this only reduces noise, the data stays untrusted.
- Resolve the PR through the API, not the artifact: `gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&head=$HEAD_OWNER:$HEAD_BRANCH"`, then require `.head.sha == $HEAD_SHA` and `.head.repo.full_name == $HEAD_REPO`. Pass every event field through `env:`. If the PR head has moved, post nothing.
- Permissions: score job read-only; comment job `{actions: read, pull-requests: write}`; leaderboard write in its own job.
- Sticky comment: match marker `<!-- topple-ci:v1 -->` AND `user.login == 'github-actions[bot]'`.
- Artifact intake: `GET /actions/runs/{id}/artifacts`, and reject if there is more than one artifact, the name is unexpected, or size_in_bytes > 20 MB. Download the zip over REST into an empty `$RUNNER_TEMP/untrusted`. Extract with Python zipfile against an allow-list (results.json, traj_000..019.npz, out_000..019.txt), with per-member size caps and no directories or symlinks.
- Concurrency: `group: publish-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.id }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}`. Using it as a key is fine; never pass it to a shell.
issues.evidence:
- GitHub community discussion #25220 (pull_requests empty for fork PRs).
- GitHub changelog 2026-06-18, 'Safer pull_request_target defaults for actions/checkout' (v7 also covers workflow_run).
- GHSA-6q32-hq47-5qq3 (CVE-2024-42471).

issues.title: The container uid separation can't work as specified (--cap-drop ALL + --user 65534)
issues.recommendation:
**Option B (recommended for Phase 3):** the host runs outside, or in its own pinned container. Each episode runs only the child in a fresh `docker run --rm --init --network none --read-only --user 65534:65534 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges ... -v sub:/submission:ro -v ep_fifos:/ipc`. The protocol goes over two FIFOs in a bind-mounted directory, which are direct kernel pipes, or over `docker run -i` stdio.
- Gives a fresh /tmp and guaranteed process cleanup per episode, with no capability juggling.
- Costs roughly 0.3–1 s of container start per episode. I couldn't measure this because the docker daemon was not running here.

**Option A (faster):** `--user 0:0 --cap-drop ALL --cap-add SETUID --cap-add SETGID --cap-add KILL`.
- The host spawns the child with `Popen(..., user=65534, group=65534, extra_groups=[], umask=0o077, start_new_session=True, close_fds=True, pass_fds=(r, w), env=MIN_ENV)`, never preexec_fn.
- The host calls prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0).
- Results go to a directory the child can't write: a bind mount created with `sudo install -d -o 0 -g 0 -m 0700`, or a tar streamed on the host's stdout.
- The salt comes from stdin or a 0400 root-owned file and is wiped after reading.
- After every episode and before writing results, a uid-65534 reaper runs kill(-1, SIGKILL) and removes its own /tmp files; then the host waits until no uid-65534 task remains.

In both options, nightly and the trusted re-run run the untrusted controller in a job with no write permissions.
issues.evidence: Linux credential rules (setuid needs CAP_SETUID; signalling another uid needs CAP_KILL; /proc environ and fd access is PTRACE_MODE_READ, which Yama does not block for the same uid). Not exercised in a container: the docker daemon was unavailable.

issues.title: Scores change with isolation mode unless the host sends float32-rounded observations
issues.problem: In-process, run_episode passes the controller `BalancerObs.from_array(<the env's float32 obs>)`. The design advertises the "lossless 88-byte wire format". If the runner serializes the env's internal float64 BalancerObs instead, out-of-process controllers see different numbers and the trajectory diverges. That breaks "results must not depend on isolation" and the contract §14 statement that traj `obs` (f4) is exactly what the controller received.
issues.recommendation:
- Define one helper, e.g. `controller_obs(obs_arr, t) = BalancerObs.from_array(float32 row, t)`, used by every path. The wire carries `controller_obs(...).to_wire()`: the float32 values, widened exactly to f64.
- State in contract §6 that features are float32-quantized.
- Add a parity test: PID, LQR, random and the PPO ONNX policy on all 20 public seeds must give byte-identical traj ctrl and qpos, and identical results.json apart from `isolation`, for inprocess vs subprocess. Run the same check against container in CI.

issues.title: Per-call limits alone let one submission stall CI past the job timeout, and RLIMIT_CPU is ignorable on macOS
issues.recommendation:
Add a frozen `runner:` block to challenge.yaml:
- load_s: 10 (spawn to INIT ok; onnxruntime import + session measured at 67 ms)
- reset_s: 1
- act_s: 0.25, as a hang detector
- episode_act_budget_s: 5 (sum of act waits; 5 ms per step on average, about 200× an ONNX MLP round trip)
- episode_wall_s: 30
- eval_wall_s: 150
- cpu_s: 20 (RLIMIT_CPU soft == hard)

Behaviour:
- When eval_wall_s is exceeded, the remaining episodes get `timeout` and results are still written with complete=false.
- Fail fast: if episode 0 ends in load_error or a load timeout, record the same error for all episodes instead of spawning 19 more children.
- On macOS, the host enforces CPU itself (os.wait4 rusage, or a watchdog).
- timeout-minutes 10 stays only as a backstop; with N submissions per PR, N × eval_wall_s must fit inside it (N ≤ 3).
- Keep every budget at least 10× above the honest p99 measured on the runner, so timing never changes an honest score.
issues.evidence:
rlimit_probe.py on macOS:
- RLIMIT_CPU soft = hard = 1 s with a busy loop: killed by SIGXCPU.
- Same limit with SIGXCPU ignored: 'still alive after 4.0 s CPU'.

issues.title: Host I/O must be non-blocking with one deadline-driven poll loop and an exit fd (blocking write hangs at step 736)
issues.problem:
- A child that writes replies without reading requests fills the host-to-child pipe: 65,504 B on macOS, which is 736 ACT frames. A blocking os.write then hangs the host forever, and read timeouts never fire.
- If stderr is not drained, a chatty child blocks at about 64 KiB and is misreported as `timeout` instead of `output_limit`.
- A grandchild that inherited the reply fd hides the child's death (no EOF), so a crash becomes a slow `timeout`.
- Python ignores SIGPIPE, so a write to a dead child raises BrokenPipeError; that must map to `crash`.
issues.recommendation:
- Set O_NONBLOCK on the host's pipe ends.
- Run one poll() over {reply_fd, out_fd, exit_fd}, with one monotonic deadline per operation. exit_fd is os.pidfd_open(pid) on Linux 5.3+; on macOS use kqueue KQ_FILTER_PROC with NOTE_EXIT, or Popen.poll() every 20 ms.
- Write only when POLLOUT is ready, under the same deadline. Drain out_fd on every wakeup.
- Enforce strict lockstep: after a complete reply, poll(0) on reply_fd must show no bytes, otherwise the episode ends with `protocol`. This catches the pre-write attack at step 1.
- The child bootstrap marks its fds CLOEXEC and exits on EOF. On Linux it also sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) and re-checks getppid().
- Never use communicate() or wait for EOF after a kill.
- Keep pipe_hang_probe as a regression test.

Poll-style I/O costs almost nothing: p50 8.0 µs vs 7.2 µs blocking (raw), 15.0 µs vs 15.2 µs with PID.
issues.evidence:
- pipe_hang_probe.py: 'pipe capacity: 65504 bytes = 736 ACT frames', then 'host blocked in os.write() at step 736'.
- ipc_bench.py: blocking vs poll numbers above.

issues.title: The done-when can't be reached as written: private-repo permissions, fork-run approval, default-branch rule
issues.problem:
The repo stays private during Phase 3.
- With `permissions: {}`, GITHUB_TOKEN can't read contents, so actions/checkout fails on a private repo. Pulling a private GHCR image also needs `packages: read` plus repository access on the package. I'm confident about checkout; I have not verified the GHCR + fork-token combination.
- Private repos need "Run workflows from fork pull requests" enabled (Settings → Actions → General). I believe it is off by default.
- Public repos: per GitHub docs, "by default, all first-time contributors require approval to run workflows".
- workflow_run only triggers for workflow files on the default branch, so publish.yml can't be exercised from the phase-3 branch.
- A failed or cancelled eval run produces no comment at all.
issues.recommendation:
- eval.yml: `permissions: {contents: read}`, plus `packages: read` while the image is private (or make the package public at release).
- Merge publish.yml to main first (it does nothing until eval.yml exists), or run the end-to-end test on a throwaway public repo.
- Define the metric: start at the PR opened/synchronize event, or at approval for first-time contributors; stop at the comment's updated_at; take the median of 5 runs. Print queue, eval and publish times in the comment footer.
- Post an error comment whenever the eval run's conclusion != success.
- Keep the eval image small (no OSMesa, LLVM or imageio-ffmpeg; render only in publish) and cache uv in publish.

Compute is not the issue. Measured on M5 Pro: eval 1.8–2.0 s, 20 child spawns 0.9–1.35 s, IPC 0.2–1.0 s, verify 1.6 s, GIF 2.6 s at 25 fps. Even 3× slower on a 2-vCPU runner that is about 25 s. The rest of the 180 s goes to two runner acquisitions, image pull, dependency install and workflow_run dispatch, so measure those.
issues.evidence:
- GitHub docs, 'Managing GitHub Actions settings for a repository' (first-time contributor approval default).
- GitHub docs, 'Events that trigger workflows' (workflow_run requires the file on the default branch).
- startup_bench.py, determinism_probe.py, forge_probe.py (timings).

issues.title: RLIMIT_AS=1 GiB can't be set on macOS, risks breaking ONNX on Linux, and the cgroup memory policy is incomplete
issues.problem:
**macOS:** setrlimit for RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA at 512 MiB raises ValueError, because a bare python already has a 466 GiB virtual size. A 1 GiB allocation then succeeds. A memory-bomb red-team test run on a dev Mac would push it into swap.

**Linux** (unmeasured; docker daemon down): RLIMIT_AS counts address-space reservations, such as glibc arenas (64 MiB per thread), OpenBLAS per-thread buffers and ORT arenas, so python+numpy+onnxruntime can approach 1 GiB of virtual size. The Phase 2 PPO ONNX policy, the natural done-when controller, could then fail as `load_error` only in CI.

Other gaps:
- MAP_SHARED anonymous memory and tmpfs pages escape RLIMIT_DATA.
- With the default --memory-swap (twice --memory), a memory bomb swaps and ends as a timeout instead of a clean OOM.
- The cgroup OOM killer may pick the host.
issues.recommendation:
- Linux child: RLIMIT_DATA = 1 GiB with soft == hard (not RLIMIT_AS), set by the bootstrap before importing user code. The child also writes 1000 to /proc/self/oom_score_adj so the OOM killer picks it.
- Container: `--memory 2g --memory-swap 2g`, and an explicit `size=` on every tmpfs.
- Measure VmPeak and VmData of the PPO policy inside the image and keep the limits at least 2× above that.
- macOS: either an RSS watchdog (proc_pid_rusage ri_phys_footprint via ctypes, or `ps -o rss=` every 100 ms), or declare memory limits unsupported locally and mark memory- and fork-bomb tests container-only.
- Rename "RSS 1 GiB" to what is actually enforced.
issues.evidence:
rlimit_probe.py:
- RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA both report 'setrlimit failed: ValueError current limit exceeds maximum limit | ALLOCATED 1GiB'.
- Bare python virtual size: 488,745,680 KiB.

issues.title: Verify in the eval's exact environment; child numerics vary across runner CPUs
issues.problem:
Host physics goes through libm, both inside MuJoCo and via Python's math module (e.g. math.cos/sin of yaw sets the push direction in push_force_world). Evaluating in a Debian-based python:3.12-slim image but verifying with `uv run` on ubuntu-24.04, which has a different glibc, is not guaranteed bit-exact. Honest submissions could then fail verification.

GitHub-hosted x64 runners also mix CPUs with and without AVX-512. numpy's SIMD dispatch and onnxruntime's MLAS kernels are chosen at runtime by CPU, so actions can differ in the last bit between hosts. Re-runs of the same ONNX policy (PR vs nightly) can then diverge.
issues.recommendation:
- Pick one physics environment, the digest-pinned image, and run eval, verify/rescore, render and nightly inside it.
- Record the image digest in results.versions and refuse to verify across different digests.
- In the child environment, set NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES="AVX512F AVX512CD AVX512_SKX AVX512_CLX AVX512_CNL AVX512_ICL AVX512_SPR" and OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell. I don't know of an equivalent knob for onnxruntime MLAS; check.
- Document that a run's recorded ctrl is authoritative and that re-runs of float-heavy controllers may differ slightly.
issues.evidence: Not measured; no x86 Linux was available. Based on reading python/topple/disturbances.py (math.cos/sin in push_force_world) and known library dispatch behaviour.

issues.title: Process-tree cleanup and pid accounting: killpg isn't enough, and --pids-limit is shared with the host
issues.problem:
- A grandchild that calls setsid() escapes killpg.
- Without --init, orphaned zombies accumulate under PID 1 and count toward pids.max.
- --pids-limit 128 is shared by host and child. A fork bomb in episode k can stop the host from spawning the next child, or even creating a thread, which is not a clean failure.
- A lingering process can carry state into later episodes through /tmp, which breaks "no state leaks between episodes".
- On Linux, RLIMIT_NPROC counts threads per real uid. In subprocess mode, where the child shares the user's uid, a low value blocks numpy and onnxruntime thread creation. On macOS it counts processes only: RLIMIT_NPROC=64 made fork fail with EAGAIN while threads still worked.
issues.recommendation:
Container:
- `--init` and `--pids-limit 256`.
- Child runs as uid 65534 with RLIMIT_NPROC = 64, which must exceed the child's thread count. The host keeps at least 190 pids of headroom.
- After each episode, a uid-65534 reaper calls kill(-1, SIGKILL), which only reaches sandbox processes. It also deletes the episode's TMPDIR. The host then waits until no uid-65534 task remains. Option B (one container per episode) gives all of this for free.

Subprocess mode on Linux:
- The host sets PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, so escaped descendants are reparented to it.
- After each episode it kills and reaps every descendant listed in /proc/<host>/task/*/children.
- Never set RLIMIT_NPROC there.

macOS: killpg is best effort; document the gap.

Every episode gets a fresh TMPDIR and HOME, deleted afterwards.
issues.evidence: rlimit_probe.py on macOS: 'RLIMIT_NPROC=64 → fork failed: [Errno 35] Resource temporarily unavailable | thread OK'.

issues.title: `python -I` silently disables PYTHONHASHSEED; launch the child with -s -P -B and an explicit minimal env
issues.problem:
`-I` implies `-E`, so a PYTHONHASHSEED passed by the host is ignored and string hashing is randomized in every child. A controller that accumulates floats while iterating a set or dict of strings then produces different actions per process.

Inheriting os.environ would also pass CI and job variables into untrusted code.

Without thread caps, numpy, OpenBLAS and onnxruntime size their thread pools from os.cpu_count(). That ignores --cpus, oversubscribes the CFS quota and causes latency spikes.
issues.evidence:
hashseed_probe.sh, the same 3-line accumulation over a set of strings:
- Under -I, 8 runs print 0.0 or 1.0 at random.
- Under -s -P with PYTHONHASHSEED=0, the result is stable.
- hash('kp') differs on every -I run.

issues.title: In-process and out-of-process runs differ beyond observations: module state, error codes, BaseException, FP environment
issues.problem:
- **Module state:** load_submission imports the module once and reuses the factory for all 20 episodes. Module-level state carries across episodes in-process but not with one child per episode. With a module-level random.Random(42), 19 of 20 episodes scored differently.
- **Error codes:** in-process, an import failure aborts the CLI with exit 2 and no results.json, while a child would report `load_error`. A LoadError raised inside _wrap_factory is recorded as `exception`.
- **BaseException:** sys.exit() or KeyboardInterrupt in act escapes `except Exception` and kills the whole in-process eval; in a child the same thing is a `crash`.
- **FP environment:** an in-process controller can change the host's floating-point mode and therefore the physics. A library built with -ffast-math sets FTZ/DAZ when loaded, and fesetround is reachable via ctypes.
- **Shared TaskSpec:** TaskSpec.extras is one mutable dict shared by every episode.
- **Sibling imports:** importing helper modules from a directory submission is undefined, because spec_from_file_location doesn't put the directory on sys.path.
issues.recommendation:
- Write one normative table mapping each failure event to its code, step and detail format. Implement it once and use it in both paths.
- In-process: re-exec the submission module into a fresh module object per episode. Catch BaseException and map SystemExit to `crash`. Wrap extras in MappingProxyType.
- Pick one sibling-import policy for both modes; I recommend prepending the submission directory to sys.path.
- Document in-process runs as development-only, never rankable.
- Add a parity matrix test: every failure kind × every isolation mode must give identical results.json apart from `isolation`.
issues.evidence: module_state_probe.py: 'episodes with different scores: 19/20; aggregate inprocess=71.904 vs per-episode-process=71.868'.

issues.title: The wire protocol needs length framing, a handshake, per-op size caps and status codes
issues.problem:
A request of `<B` op + payload has no length field. The variable-length INIT JSON and error details therefore can't be framed.

There is no READY handshake, so a bootstrap failure can't be told apart from a user import failure.

Reply status values, maximum sizes and the handling of extra or partial bytes are undefined.
issues.recommendation:
Headers: request `<BI` (op, payload_len as u32 LE); reply `<BI` (status, len).

Handshake: after setting its limits and before importing user code, the child sends READY (0x10) with payload `<HH` (proto_major, proto_minor).

Ops:
- INIT 0x01: TaskSpec JSON, at most 4096 B. Reply OK 0x00 (len 0) or ERR 0x01.
- RESET 0x02: payload `<Q`.
- ACT 0x03: exactly 88 B. Reply OK with exactly 16 B `<2d`.
- CLOSE 0x04: len 0, no reply. The host waits at most 1 s, then SIGKILL.

ERR payload: one `<B` code (1 exception, 2 invalid_action, 3 load_error) followed by UTF-8 detail of at most 1024 B. The host decodes with errors='replace', strips C0/C1 and ANSI sequences, and truncates to 300 chars (results.MAX_DETAIL_CHARS).

The child runs validate_action before packing, so honest children produce the same codes and details as in-process.

The host treats any of these as `protocol`: an unknown status, a length above the op's cap, non-finite floats in an OK reply, or unsolicited bytes.

Record runner_protocol "1" in results.versions.
issues.evidence: Design text, section 1.

issues.title: Output policy: decide where stdout goes, what the 64 KiB cap does, and how untrusted text is sanitized
issues.problem:
Only stderr is mentioned.
- If stdout is inherited, a controller can flood the Actions log.
- If hitting the cap kills the child, an honest controller printing 100 B per step (100 KB per episode) scores 0 with `output_limit`.
- Untrusted text echoed into a trusted job's log can inject workflow commands (::add-mask::, ::error::, ::stop-commands::).
- In PR comments it can @mention people, cross-reference issues, or break the markdown.
issues.recommendation:
- The bootstrap dup2s fd 1 onto fd 2, so one pipe carries both streams.
- The host keeps the first 32 KiB and the last 32 KiB per episode and counts the total. It kills with `output_limit` only above 8 MiB per episode.
- Save the kept text as an `out_NNN.txt` artifact.
- Never print it in a trusted job's log. If that is unavoidable, wrap it in `::stop-commands::<random hex>` … `::<token>::`.
- In comments: escape backticks and put the text in code fences; insert U+200B after '@' and '#'; cap the comment body at 60k chars (GitHub's limit is 65,536).

issues.title: Subprocess isolation is not a security boundary; scope the red-team claims and the CLI default
issues.recommendation:
- Document subprocess mode as crash and hang containment for code you trust.
- Default to subprocess for all paths, and print a warning when the path is outside the current git repo.
- Run hostile red-team cases only under a `container` pytest marker: skipped unless docker answers, and run by a required CI job.
- For trying someone else's controller, point users to `--isolation container` or the browser Arena.
- Copy the submission into a private temp directory, hash the copy, and import from that copy.

issues.title: The red-team list is incomplete; give each case an expected outcome and the layer that enforces it
issues.problem: The design lists about 17 cases with no expected error codes and no isolation mode. Several attack classes the design must withstand are missing.
issues.recommendation:
**Child cases** (expected code; host stays alive; total wall time within budget):
1. Infinite loop or sleep at import, in make_controller, or in reset → timeout plus fail-fast.
2. Sleep 0.2 s per act → per-episode budget timeout.
3. Background CPU-burning thread while act returns quickly → RLIMIT_CPU.
4. Memory, each case → MemoryError, cgroup OOM kill or ENOSPC, with the host surviving:
   - fast bytearray of 4 GiB;
   - slow growth of 10 MB per step;
   - MAP_SHARED anonymous mmap of 4 GiB;
   - filling the /tmp tmpfs.
5. Fork bomb, thread bomb (10k threads), and a double-forked setsid() daemon that outlives the episode → contained, then reaped before the next episode.
6. os.system or subprocess spawning sh → fails or is contained.
7. Network: TCP to 1.1.1.1:443, DNS lookup, UDP, the metadata address 169.254.169.254, and /var/run/docker.sock (must not exist).
8. Filesystem writes to /, to /submission, to the output directory, and a .pth into site-packages → denied.
9. Reading /proc/<host>/{environ,cmdline,fd/*}, the salt file, or /run/secrets → denied, and the salt must not appear in argv.
10. Signals: kill(getppid, SIGKILL or SIGSTOP), kill(-1, SIGKILL), killpg(0); SIGSTOP on itself → timeout.
11. Crashes: ctypes segfault, os.abort, os._exit mid-episode, sys.exit in act, deep recursion → crash, with no core file.
12. 10k open fds → EMFILE.
13. Output: 1 GB on stdout or stderr, no newlines, ANSI codes, ::workflow-command:: lines, NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8, @mentions and HTML.
14. Bad actions: NaN, inf, strings, bytes, None, dict, 1 or 3 values, a 2-D ndarray, numpy bool, complex, Fraction, an object whose __float__ sleeps or raises, a list of 10^8 items → same codes in every mode.
15. Protocol abuse: replying before a request, pre-writing 1000 replies, a partial frame then a stall, a length field of 4 GiB, an unknown status, closing or dup2-ing over the protocol fds → protocol or timeout, never a host hang.
16. Nondeterminism: reading time.time, os.urandom, the global `random`, id() or hash(str) → the run still verifies.
17. Monkeypatching topple inside the child → no effect on the host.
18. Seed fingerprinting → allowed, and caught by private seeds.

**Artifact and workflow cases:**
19. Forged results.json (score 100, isolation: container).
20. Oracle-generated ctrl.
21. Each forged meta field: max_steps, termination, control_dt, joint_qpos, wheel_sign, preset, challenge, episode_index.
22. Edited or swapped scenario.
23. Missing, duplicate or reordered episodes.
24. Malformed npz: extra members, object arrays, Fortran order, huge header shapes, zip bomb, ../ member names, symlinks, non-UTF-8 meta, deeply nested JSON, 1e999 in meta.
25. Artifacts larger than the cap or with unexpected names.
26. Malicious head_branch, PR title or commit message.
27. A PR number in the artifact pointing at another PR.
28. A PR that moves to a new head mid-publish.
29. A spoofed sticky-comment marker.
30. A look-alike workflow also named `eval`.
31. 50 submissions in one PR, or 100 PRs → caps, concurrency and cancel-in-progress.
32. Leaderboard names with bidi characters, homoglyphs or '|' → strict regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`.

issues.title: Leaderboard write path, provisional ranks and private-seed side channels
issues.problem:
- `contents: write` to main from a fork-triggered workflow conflicts with branch protection and widens the blast radius, and concurrent publish runs race each other.
- Public seeds are fingerprintable: the initial pitch, drawn from U(−3°, 3°), differs per seed. A controller can recognize the seed from its first observation and replay a memorized, offline-optimized sequence. That is legal and tops the public-seed ranking even with a trusted re-run.
- Nightly needs the code of PRs that were never merged, and the design doesn't say where it comes from.
- A private aggregate score rounded to 2 decimals leaks about 13 bits per night to a controller that encodes information in its own score.
issues.recommendation:
- Label ranks in PR comments "public seeds, provisional". Rank the leaderboard by nightly private scores.
- Write the leaderboard to a `leaderboard` branch, a release asset or R2, from a dedicated job with `concurrency: {group: leaderboard, cancel-in-progress: false}`.
- Key entries by (login, submission name, head_sha, submission sha256). Archive the accepted submission files where the trusted nightly can fetch them.
- Rotate private seeds per night or per season.
- The nightly job that executes code holds no write permissions; the salt goes to the host only.

issues.title: Container spec gaps, seccomp stance and the submission runtime
issues.problem:
The docker run line is missing --init, a swap cap, explicit tmpfs flags, an IPC setting and ulimits.

The image bundles OSMesa, LLVM and ffmpeg, which the eval stage doesn't need, so the pull is larger and slower.

The digest pin in eval.yml can be edited by the PR author, so it protects nothing there.

The allowed imports and dependency versions for submissions are not specified; anything outside the image (scipy, torch) will fail as `load_error`.

On Apple Silicon, `--isolation container` runs linux/arm64, which is not the CI platform.
issues.recommendation:
- Add `--init --memory-swap 2g --tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,size=64m,mode=1777 --ipc none --ulimit core=0 --ulimit nofile=256:256`.
- Use `--pull never` after an explicit `docker pull image@sha256:...`.
- Keep Docker's default seccomp profile; never use seccomp=unconfined or --privileged. Docker 25 and later also block io_uring by default; check the runner's Docker version. A custom seccomp profile isn't worth it in Phase 3; plan gVisor or Firecracker for Phase 14's hosted runner.
- Split the images: a small eval image (python:3.12-slim + mujoco + numpy + onnxruntime + topple) and a separate render image.
- Pin the digest in default-branch workflows, where the pin actually protects something.
- Document the submission runtime (Python 3.12, plus the pinned numpy, onnxruntime and topple versions; no network, no pip) and record it in results.versions.
- Label local Apple Silicon container results as platform linux-aarch64, or offer `--platform linux/amd64`.
- On Ubuntu runners, check whether core_pattern pipes to apport; it should honour RLIMIT_CORE=0. I have not verified this.

issues.title: IPC isn't the bottleneck; avoid tight act timeouts and trim child start-up
issues.problem:
Per-step IPC is cheap: 20k round trips cost 0.2–1.0 s. Tail wake-up latency is what matters: with simulated physics between steps, macOS showed p99.9 up to 2.3 ms and a max of 26.6 ms. On Linux, CFS quota throttling can stall a process for up to about one 100 ms period when busy threads exceed --cpus. An act timeout below about 100 ms would produce spurious timeouts.

Child start-up has avoidable cost. `import topple.contract` takes 46 ms against 21 ms for a bare `python -I`, because topple/__init__ imports importlib.metadata (about 19 ms) and runs _gl.configure() inside the child.
issues.recommendation:
- Keep act_s at 0.25 s or more.
- Set --cpus to the runner's vCPU count, and evaluate one submission per container, one at a time.
- Make topple/__init__ lazy: provide __version__ through a PEP 562 `__getattr__`, and call _configure_gl() only when mujoco is imported (envs/rendering). Untrusted children and lesson-1 submissions then start in about 25 ms.
- Don't use a zygote or fork server: forking after threads is unsafe, and the snapshot leaks state between episodes. 20 spawns at about 50–150 ms each fit the budget.
issues.evidence: ipc_bench.py (p50/p99/max per mode); startup_bench.py: bare -I 21.1 ms, import topple.contract 46.1 ms, import numpy 48.4 ms, import onnxruntime 66.2 ms, onnxruntime + session 67.4 ms, mujoco 94.1 ms.

issues.title: Reusable action pitfalls
issues.recommendation:
- Pass inputs through `env:`; never interpolate `${{ inputs.* }}` inside run steps. Pin inner actions by SHA.
- Document `pull_request` only. Never use pull_request_target; for comments, copy the workflow_run split.
- On macOS runners, fall back to `isolation: subprocess` (trusted code only).
- Confine MJCF includes and asset paths to the repository and cap mesh sizes.
- When community challenges arrive (Phase 9), compile untrusted MJCF only inside the sandbox, never in the trusted host.

issues.title: Hashing the limits into the protocol makes every later tweak a balance-v2 bump
issues.problem: Timeouts and memory caps can change a fixed controller's score. Under contract §13, any change to them after launch requires a new challenge major version.
issues.recommendation: Freeze generous values in the challenge.yaml `runner:` block before Season 0 and include them in protocol_hash. Keep presentation-only settings (GIF fps, how much output text is retained) out of the hash.
